brief: Array a (1<=a_i<=n) is good if no i<j has a_j = a_i+1. Find the minimum number of deletions to make it good (sum n <= 3e5).
key_idea: Only values v and v+1 interact: every kept v+1 must come before every kept v, so DP value by value with state = first kept position of v.
solution:
1. Maximize kept count; answer = n - kept.
2. Kept copies of v must all lie before the first kept copy of v-1 and after the last kept copy of v+1, so for v keep a contiguous block of its occurrence list.
3. State dp[v][j] = best kept count over values 1..v when the first kept v is its j-th occurrence; plus dp[v][none] = best overall of v-1 (keep no v).
4. Transition: dp[v][j] = max over prev states s of v-1 (first position pos_s, or INF for none) of dp_s + cnt(v-occurrences < pos_s) - j, needing cnt > j. Sort candidates by cnt and use suffix max + pointer.
5. Answer n - max over states of the last value.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
dry_run:
Sample 1 2 3 4 5: each value has 1 occurrence; v=2 with v=1 kept conflicts (2 after 1).
Best alternates values: keep 1,3,5 -> kept 3.
Answer 5-3 = 2 (matches).
Sample 5 5 5 4 4: all 4's after 5's is fine (4 then 5 forbidden only) -> 0.

brief: n x m board (nm <= 3e5) with white cells; each white cell colored red or blue. Value of a coloring = max dominoes where horizontal dominoes cover two red cells and vertical ones two blue cells. Sum values over all 2^w colorings mod 998244353.
key_idea: Rows and columns are independent: a red horizontal run contributes floor(len/2), counted greedily as 'pair ends at cell j when the red streak ending at j has even length'.
solution:
1. Horizontal dominoes only use red, vertical only blue, so total = sum over horizontal runs + vertical runs.
2. In a run, greedy left-to-right pairing: a domino ends at cell j iff cells ...j are red with an even-length streak ending at j.
3. f[j] = #colorings of j cells with even red streak (>=2) ending at j = [j even] + sum over even t<j of 2^(j-t-1); recurrence S[j]=2S[j-1]+[j-1 even].
4. Each such ending at position j of a run contributes f[j]*2^(w-j) (other cells free). Precompute G[L] = sum_{j=2..L} f[j]*2^(w-j).
5. Answer = sum of G[L] over all maximal horizontal and vertical white runs.
dry_run:

f[2]=1, f[3]=1, f[4]=3.
G[4]=1*4 + 1*2 + 3*1 = 9.
Vertical runs have length 1 -> 0. Answer 9 (matches).

brief: Connected multigraph, each vertex has d_i in {-1,0,1}. Choose an edge subset so every vertex with d_i != -1 has degree parity d_i; print any or -1.
key_idea: Work on a spanning tree: process leaves up, take the parent edge when a vertex's parity is wrong; the root's parity is forced, fixable only via a -1 vertex.
solution:
1. If no d_i = -1 and sum of d_i is odd -> -1 (sum of degrees is even).
2. Set every -1 to 0, but if the sum is odd set one -1 vertex to 1.
3. Build a DFS/BFS spanning tree from vertex 1.
4. Process vertices in reverse visit order (children before parents): if d[u]==1 take edge to parent and flip d[parent].
5. Root ends correct because total parity is even. Print chosen edge indices.

Vertex 3: d=1 -> take edge3, d1=1. Vertex 2: d=1 -> take edge1, d1=0.
Output edges {1,3}: deg1=2,deg3=1 valid (any answer accepted).

brief: Timeline 1..n, k envelopes (s,t,d,w): collectable in [s,t], then Bob is busy until d. Bob greedily takes max w (tie max d). Alice may disturb at most m <= 200 moments; minimize Bob's total coins.
key_idea: Bob's choice at each time x is fixed (precompute with a multiset sweep); then dp[x][j] = min coins from time x having used j disturbances.
solution:
1. Sweep x=1..n: add envelopes with s=x into a multiset of (w,d), take the max as Bob's pick W[x],D[x]; remove envelopes whose t=x after.
2. If nothing available: W[x]=0, D[x]=x.
3. dp[x][j] = min(W[x] + dp[D[x]+1][j], dp[x+1][j+1] if j<m).
4. Base dp[n+1][*]=0; answer dp[1][0]. Use long long.
complexity: O(k log k + n*m) time, O(n*m) space
dry_run:

Disturb at 1: dp[2][1] = 2 + dp[7][1] = 2.
No disturb: 4 + dp[3][0] = 4+3+5+7+9 ... larger.
Answer 2 (matches).

brief: Walk from 0 to a (a <= 2000); some unit segments are rainy and need an umbrella. m umbrellas at x_i with weight p_i; each unit costs the total weight carried. Minimum fatigue or -1.
key_idea: Carry at most one umbrella: dp[x][k] = min fatigue at position x holding umbrella k (0 = none).
solution:
1. Mark rain[x] for segment [x,x+1]; for each point keep the lightest umbrella there.
2. At position x let mn = min over dp[x][*]; you may switch to the lightest umbrella at x (dp = mn) or drop (dp[x][0] = mn).
3. Move: dp[x+1][k] = dp[x][k] + w_k, forbidden for k=0 on rainy segments.
4. Answer min dp[a][*], -1 if INF.

At x=9 drop -> dp[0]=45, last unit dry.
Answer 45 (matches); sample 3 umbrella at 1 -> segment [0,1] impossible -> -1.

brief: Tree; robot starts at v != 1 with p coins. Odd steps move toward vertex 1; on even steps you either pay a coin to move toward 1 or move to a uniformly random neighbour. For each query (v,p) output the minimum expected steps (mod 998244353).
key_idea: Split the path into (odd step into u, even step at u) blocks: a random block at u costs 2*deg(u) in expectation, a paid one costs 2, so pay for the p largest degrees.
solution:
1. Root the tree at 1 (BFS parents). Path v=w0,w1,...,wL=1.
2. Even steps happen at w1,w3,... (excluding vertex 1). For block at u: E = 1 + E_even, E_even = 1 + (deg-1)/deg*(1+E_even) -> E_even = 2deg-1, so block = 2*deg(u).
3. Paying a coin makes the block cost exactly 2.
4. Sort block costs descending; first p get cost 2, others 2*deg. Add 1 if L is odd (final odd step into 1).
5. Answer is an integer; print mod 998244353. sum n,q <= 2000 so O(n log n) per query is fine.
complexity: O(q * n log n) time, O(n) space
dry_run:

Query (3,0): path 3,2,1, L=2; block at 2, deg 3 -> 6.
Query (3,1): pay the coin -> 2.
Query (2,0): L=1, no blocks, +1 -> 1. All match.

brief: n people with a_i candies; each person gives at most once (2^x candies to someone) and receives at most once. Can everyone end equal? (n <= 2e5)
key_idea: d_i = a_i - avg must be 2^a - 2^b; |d| = 2^k persons are flexible (single gift or 2^(k+1)-2^k), so balance give/receive counts bit by bit from low to high.
solution:
1. If sum % n != 0 -> No. d_i = a_i - avg; d=0 persons are irrelevant.
2. If |d| is not a power of two it must equal 2^h - 2^l uniquely (lo = lowbit, hi = |d|+lo must be a power of two) else No; add mandatory give/receive to net[h], net[l].
3. If |d| = 2^k: default single gift; net[k] += sign; count pos[k]/neg[k].
4. For b = 0..37: net[b] must be even; if net>0 convert net/2 of the +2^b persons (each changes net[b] by -2 and net[b+1] by +1), if net<0 convert from -2^b persons; not enough -> No.
5. All bits balanced -> Yes.
complexity: O(n + 32) time per test, O(1) extra space
dry_run:
Sample 1: a=2 4 3, avg 3, d=-1,+1,0.
net[0] = +1 - 1 = 0; all bits zero.
Answer Yes (matches).
Sample 3: 1 4 7 1 5 4 avg 11/3 not integer... sum 22 %6 != 0 -> No (matches).

brief: Rooted tree (n up to 1e6). Find the minimum depth d of a perfect binary tree that can be turned into the given tree by repeatedly contracting a vertex into its parent.
key_idea: f(v) from children depths: one child -> f(c)+1; else the smallest d with sum 2^{f(c)} <= 2^d, computed by repeatedly merging the two smallest exponents a<=b into b+1.
solution:
1. Process vertices from n down to 1 (parents have smaller index).
2. Leaf: f=0.
3. One child: f = f(child)+1 (the root must still have two children).
4. Several children: min-heap of f(c); pop two smallest a<=b, push b+1 (rounding 2^a up to 2^b is safe since the total is a multiple of 2^b); last value is f(v).
5. Answer f(1).
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
dry_run:
Test 3: 1->2, 2->{3,4,5} leaves.
f(2): heap {0,0,0} -> {0,1} -> {2}; f(2)=2.
f(1): single child -> 3.
Answer 3 (matches).

brief: A WASD command string moves a robot; Grid(s) is the smallest rectangle containing the walk. Insert at most one extra W/A/S/D anywhere to minimize the area (|s| <= 2e5).
key_idea: Axes are independent; an axis range can shrink by 1 iff its range >= 2 and all max occurrences come before all min occurrences (or vice versa).
solution:
1. Build prefix positions x[0..n], y[0..n] (start 0).
2. W = range(x)+1, H = range(y)+1.
3. canShrink(axis): range >= 2 and (lastMax < firstMin or lastMin < firstMax); inserting the opposite move right after the last extreme shifts the rest.
4. Answer min(W*H, (W-1)*H if canShrink(x), W*(H-1) if canShrink(y)). Use long long.

y: min idx2-3 before max idx7 -> 3*3=9.
Answer 8 (matches).

brief: Cost of a regular bracket sequence = min total cost to erase it by removing adjacent '()' pairs, each costing the number of brackets to its right. With at most k <= 5 moves (take one bracket and reinsert it), keeping it regular, minimize the cost.
key_idea: Cost = sum over matched pairs of the number of pairs nested inside it; one move puts a '(' just before its ')', removing exactly that pair's inside count, so subtract the k largest.
solution:
1. Match brackets with a stack; for pair (o,i) inside count c = (i-o-1)/2.
2. Total cost = sum of all c (each pair is erased after everything inside it... equivalently sum of depths).
3. A move turning a pair into '()' decreases cost by its c; choices are independent.
4. Sort c descending and subtract the top k. Use long long.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

brief: Directed graph with vertex values; take its transitive closure H. Output the maximum number of vertices on a simple path in H and the minimum value sum among such longest paths.
key_idea: In the closure every SCC can be fully walked, so condense SCCs (weight = size, cost = value sum) and do longest-path DP on the DAG with tie-break on minimum sum.
solution:
1. Find SCCs (Kosaraju/Tarjan, iterative to avoid deep recursion).
2. For each SCC: sz = #vertices, sm = sum of a_i.
3. Build the condensation DAG; process components in reverse topological order.
4. best[c] = (sz[c] + L, sm[c] + S) where (L,S) is the successor with max L, ties min S (or (0,0)).
5. Answer = lexicographically (max length, min sum) over all best[c]. Use long long.

brief: Permutation of n balls (n <= 500). With k zero-balls inserted anywhere, each move takes a ball adjacent to a zero and puts it anywhere (cost 1). For each k=1..n output the minimum cost to sort.
key_idea: Kept balls form an increasing subsequence; every maximal block of removed balls between kept ones needs one zero, and cost = number of removed balls.
solution:
1. Add sentinels c[0]=0, c[n+1]=n+1.
2. dp[i][j] = min removed count when ball i is kept and j blocks have been removed so far.
3. dp[i][j + (p<i-1)] = min over p<i with c[p]<c[i] of dp[p][j] + (i-p-1).
4. Answer for k = min over j<=k of dp[n+1][j] (prefix minimum).

brief: n x n matrix (n <= 2000), q <= 1e6 queries: flatten a submatrix row by row into A and output sum A_i * i (1-based).
key_idea: Index of (i,j) is (i-x1)*w + (j-y1+1), linear in i and j, so 2D prefix sums of M, M*i and M*j answer each query in O(1).
solution:
1. Build 2D prefix sums P (M), PI (M*i), PJ (M*j).
2. For a query, w = y2-y1+1; S, SI, SJ = rectangle sums.
3. Answer = w*(SI - x1*S) + (SJ - (y1-1)*S).
4. Fits in long long (max ~8e18); use fast I/O for 1e6 queries.

brief: Color each of n <= 40 digits red or black so the red number is divisible by A, the black by B (A,B <= 40), both colors used; minimize |#red - #black|, print a coloring or -1.
key_idea: Reachability DP over (digit index, red mod A, black mod B, red count) with backtracking.
solution:
1. vis[i][ra][rb][r]: after i digits, red value mod A, black mod B, r reds is reachable.
2. Digit d: red -> ra' = (10ra+d)%A, r+1; black -> rb' = (10rb+d)%B.
3. Pick r in [1,n-1] with vis[n][0][0][r] minimizing |n-2r|; none -> -1.
4. Backtrack from the end: find a predecessor mod value that leads to the current state.
complexity: O(n^2 * A * B) time and space (~2.6e6 states)

brief: n <= 5000 towers; merging a tower into its neighbour adds heights. Minimum merges so heights are non-decreasing.
key_idea: Maximize the number of segments; f[i] uses the closest j with sum(j+1..i) >= last[j], which also gives the smallest last height.
solution:
1. Prefix sums pre.
2. f[i] = max segments for prefix i, last[i] = height of its last segment (minimal).
3. For i, scan j = i-1 down to 0; first j with pre[i]-pre[j] >= last[j] gives f[i]=f[j]+1, last[i]=pre[i]-pre[j].
4. Answer n - f[n].

brief: n <= 100 colored tiles; a path picks increasing indices; it is nice if its length is a multiple of k and each consecutive block of k tiles has one color. Count nice paths of maximum length mod 1e9+7 (empty path counts).
key_idea: dp[i] = (max blocks, count) for paths whose last block ends at tile i; the block picks k-1 more tiles of color c_i between the previous end j and i: C(cnt, k-1) ways.
solution:
1. State 0 = empty path (len 0, count 1).
2. For each i, scan j = i-1 down to 0 keeping same = #tiles of color c_i in (j, i).
3. If same >= k-1: candidate len[j]+1 with ways cnt[j]*C(same, k-1); keep max len, sum counts on ties.
4. Answer = sum of cnt[i] over states (including 0) with the overall max len.
complexity: O(n^2) per test, O(n^2) for binomials

Blocks of color 2 after it: ending at 4 (C(1,1)=1), at 5 (C(2,1)=2) -> len 2 count 3.

brief: Strings s, t (|s|,|t| <= 500). A move replaces one occurrence of t in s with dots. Find the minimum moves to remove all occurrences and the number of optimal sets of cut positions mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Let p be the first remaining occurrence at or after i; some cut q must overlap it (q in [p, p+|t|)), after which everything starting before q+|t| is gone: dp[i] = min/count over q of 1 + dp[q+|t|].
solution:
1. Mark occurrence starts occ[i] (direct compare, n,m <= 500).
2. dp[i] = (moves, ways) to kill all occurrences starting >= i; if none, (0,1).
3. p = first occurrence >= i; for each occurrence q in [p, p+m): candidate 1 + dp[q+m].moves; take min, sum ways of ties mod 1e9+7.
4. Answer dp[0].

From 0: choose q=0 or 1 then continue at q+2.

brief: Build the trie of all correct bracket sequences of length 2n (n <= 1000). Output the size of its maximum matching mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Greedy leaf-up matching on this trie matches every node at odd depth with its parent, so answer = number of trie nodes (valid prefixes) of odd length.
solution:
1. A trie node = prefix of length d with balance b that can be completed: 0 <= b <= 2n-d.
2. w[d][b] = number of such prefixes: from (d,b) add '(' if b+1 <= 2n-d-1, add ')' if b>0.
3. Answer = sum of w[d][b] over odd d, mod 1e9+7.

brief: n <= 20 cities built one per turn in random order; a monument built at turn t has range n-t+1 at the end. m <= 5e4 points with distances d(i,j). Expected number of points controlled, mod 998244353.
key_idea: Linearity of expectation; a point is missed iff each city i is built in one of the last d_ij - 1 turns; count such permutations by sorting the allowed sizes.
solution:
1. For point j, city i fails to cover it iff built at turn > n+1-d, i.e. in the last s_i = d_ij - 1 turns.
2. Sort s ascending; #bad permutations = prod over i (0-based) of max(0, s_i - i).
3. P(conquered) = 1 - bad/n!.
4. Sum over points mod p using inverse of n!.
complexity: O(m * n log n) time, O(nm) space

Point 2: d=4,4,4 -> s=3,3,3 -> bad 3*2*1=6 -> prob 0.

brief: n x m grid (<= 1000x1000), all cells free; q <= 1e4 queries flip a cell. After each query count staircases: zigzag paths (right,down,right... or down,right,down...) on free cells, single cells included.
key_idea: Count initially with DP; each flip changes the answer by the number of staircases through that cell = f1*b1 + f2*b2 - 1, found by walking the two zigzag lines in O(n+m).
solution:
1. Initial: R[i][j] = 1 + D[i][j+1], D[i][j] = 1 + R[i+1][j] (staircases starting at cell with first move right/down); ans = sum(R + D - 1).
2. Each cell lies on two maximal zigzag lines. For each line count free cells forward (f) and backward (b) from the cell, stopping at a locked cell.
3. through(cell) = f1*b1 + f2*b2 - 1 (single cell counted twice).
4. Locking: subtract through(cell) while it is still free; unlocking: free it then add through(cell). Use long long.

brief: n x m grid, start at (1,1); k treasures. You may move left/right, and up only in one of q safe columns; never down. Minimum moves to collect all treasures.
key_idea: Per treasure row you finish at its leftmost L or rightmost R; between rows go up through the nearest safe column left or right of where you stand.
solution:
1. For each row keep L[r], R[r] of treasures; skip rows with none (row 1 without treasures: L=R=1).
2. Row 1: dL = (R-1)+(R-L) (end at L), dR = R-1 (end at R).
3. Next treasure row r from end position p: for c in {nearest safe >= p, nearest safe <= p} (lower_bound): base = d + |p-c| + (r-last).
4. End at L: base + |c-R| + (R-L); end at R: base + |c-L| + (R-L).
5. Answer min(dL, dR) after the last treasure row. Use long long.
complexity: O((k + n) log q) time, O(n + q) space

brief: Split string s (n <= 5000) into pieces; a single character costs a, a piece that already occurs as a substring of the concatenation before it costs b. Minimize total cost.
key_idea: dp over prefixes plus an LCP table: mx[j] = longest piece starting at j that occurs completely inside s[0..j) = max over k<j of min(lcp(k,j), j-k).
solution:
1. lcp[k][j] = s[k]==s[j] ? lcp[k+1][j+1]+1 : 0; compute row by row (k descending) with two 1D arrays.
2. mx[j] = max over k<j of min(lcp[k][j], j-k) (the occurrence must end before j).
3. dp[0]=0; dp[j+1] = min(dp[j+1], dp[j]+a); for i in (j, j+mx[j]]: dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[j]+b).
4. Answer dp[n].

brief: n <= 20 snakes on a strip, q <= 2e5 events: snake grows right (+) or loses its left cell (-). Choose initial single-cell positions so no collisions occur; minimize the maximum cell ever occupied.
key_idea: For each ordered pair (i,j) the minimum starting distance if j sits right after i is 1 - (min prefix of (-1 per i+ , +1 per j-)); then a TSP-style bitmask DP over the left-to-right order.
solution:
1. For each pair, track cur[i][j] over events: i+ -> -1, j- -> +1; mn[i][j] = min prefix (<= 0). Required distance = 1 - mn[i][j].
2. grow[i] = number of '+' events of snake i.
3. dp[mask][last] = min start cell of last placed snake; dp[1<<i][i] = 1.
4. dp[mask|1<<j][j] = min(dp[mask][l] + 1 - mn[l][j]).
5. Answer = min over l of dp[full][l] + grow[l] (the last snake's right end at the end).
complexity: O(n*q + 2^n * n^2) time, O(2^n * n) space
dry_run:

Pair distances: putting j after i where i grows once -> distance 2, otherwise 1.
Order 2,3,1: positions 1,2,3? best total gives 3 + grow 1 = 4.

brief: A binary string is beautiful if removing exactly one block (maximal run) leaves an odd number of blocks. Count strings of length n where every given substring [l_i, r_i] is beautiful, mod 998244353.
key_idea: With k blocks you can reach k-1 (remove an end) or k-2 (remove a middle block), so beautiful <=> k >= 2 <=> the substring is not constant; count strings where no constraint interval lies inside one run.
solution:
1. ml[r] = max l over intervals ending at r.
2. f[j] = ways where a new run starts at j (f[1]=2 for the first character's choice).
3. Run [k, j-1] is valid iff every interval with r <= j-1 has l < k, i.e. k > M_j = max ml[r] for r <= j-1 (monotone).
4. f[j] = sum f[k] for k in [M_j+1, j-1] via prefix sums; answer = same sum with j = n+1.

brief: 2n bulbs, each color on exactly two. Lit bulb lights its twin; if both bulbs of a color are lit, everything between lights. Find the minimum initial set size to light all and the number of such sets (n <= 1000, sum n^2 <= 1e6).
key_idea: Split into minimal balanced segments (every color opened is closed); each needs one bulb, and a bulb works iff its color's interval closure expands to the whole segment.
solution:
1. Scan with a set of open colors; when it becomes empty a minimal segment ends -> answer size = #segments.
2. For each color in a segment, expand [L,R] = its two positions: scanning positions inside pulls in other colors' endpoints, growing L/R until stable (O(segment)).
3. good = #colors whose closure equals the segment; each gives 2 bulbs.
4. Count = product over segments of 2*good mod 998244353.

brief: Arrays a, b (n <= 5e4, values <= 1e9). Each a_i may be replaced by a different m in [1, b_i]; the GCD of every subarray (length >= 2) must stay the same. Maximize the number of replaced indices.
key_idea: Subarray GCDs are fixed iff every adjacent pair keeps g_i = gcd(a_i,a_{i+1}); new a'_i must be a multiple of L_i = lcm(g_{i-1}, g_i), so DP over a few candidates per position.
solution:
1. g_i = gcd(a_i, a_{i+1}); gcd of any longer subarray is the gcd of its pair gcds, so only adjacent pairs matter.
2. L_i = lcm(g_{i-1}, g_i) must divide a'_i.
3. Candidates for i: keep a_i (0 ops) or L_i*t for small t (t = 1..12 here), t*L_i <= b_i and != a_i (1 op).
4. dp over positions: dp[i][c] = max ops with candidate c at i, transition allowed iff gcd(prev cand, cur cand) == g_{i-1}.
5. Answer max dp[n-1][*]. (Small-t bound is a heuristic: matched samples and an exhaustive-candidate check on random small tests.)
complexity: O(n * K^2 * log V) time with K ~ 13 candidates, O(nK) space

Candidates pos1: 1(keep), 2 (t=2); pos2: 2(keep), 1, 3, 4...

Answer 2 (matches).

brief: n turns, each with cards (cost 1-3, damage). Each turn play cards with total cost <= 3; every 10th card played overall deals double damage. Maximize total damage.
key_idea: dp[j] = best damage with (cards played) mod 10 = j; per turn only 0-3 cards and a few best combos matter; if the turn crosses a multiple of 10, double the max card of the combo.
solution:
1. Per turn sort cards by cost group descending damage.
2. Options: 1 card = best of each cost; 2 cards = top two cost-1 or top cost-1 + top cost-2; 3 cards = top three cost-1. Store (sum, max).
3. For each j and option with cnt cards: new = dp[j] + sum + (j+cnt >= 10 ? max : 0) -> nd[(j+cnt)%10].
4. Also allow playing nothing. Answer max dp. Use long long.
complexity: O(sum k log k + n*10*6) time, O(k) space

brief: DAG with a single sink; each second every positive node loses 1 and sends 1 to each out-neighbour. Find the first time all values are 0, mod 998244353 (n,m <= 1000).
key_idea: After n seconds of brute simulation, any node that will ever receive flow is already positive and stays positive, so the rest is pure accumulation: answer = n + total mass reaching the sink (topological DP mod p).
solution:
1. Simulate up to n seconds exactly (with long long); if all zero at time T, print T.
2. Otherwise f[v] = a_v (after n steps) + sum of f over in-neighbours, in topological order, mod p.
3. The sink drains 1 per second continuously, so answer = (n + f[sink]) mod p.

brief: String s (n <= 2e5). f_k = max LCP of the k pieces over all splits of s into k parts. Output f_l..f_r.
key_idea: f_k >= L iff the prefix of length L has k non-overlapping occurrences (Z-function); for each L count greedily with set jumps (<= n/L jumps), harmonic total.
solution:
1. Compute Z-array (z[0]=n).
2. For L = 1..n keep a set of positions with z[i] >= L (erase positions with z = L-1 as L grows).
3. cnt(L): p=0; repeatedly take lower_bound(p), cnt++, p = pos + L.
4. best[cnt(L)] = max(best, L); f_k = max over c >= k of best[c] (suffix max); 0 if none.
complexity: O(n log^2 n) time, O(n) space

brief: For each x in 1..k (k <= 1e5) count arrays of length 1..n (n <= 9e8) with elements in [1,k] and product x, mod 998244353.
key_idea: At most 16 elements are > 1; count ordered factorizations g[j][x] into j factors >= 2, then place the 1s: sum over lengths of C(len, j) = C(n+1, j+1).
solution:
1. g[1][x] = 1 for x >= 2; g[j][x*y] += g[j-1][x] for y >= 2 (harmonic loop), j <= 17.
2. Hockey stick: sum_{len=1..n} C(len, j) = C(n+1, j+1), computed with j+1 factors and a modular inverse.
3. ans[1] = n; ans[x] = sum_j g[j][x] * C(n+1, j+1).
complexity: O(k log k * 17) time, O(17k) space

brief: Given d <= 500 and s <= 5000, print the smallest positive integer divisible by d with digit sum s, or -1.
key_idea: BFS over states (remainder mod d, digit sum) appending digits 0..9 in increasing order: first time reaching (0, s) gives the shortest and lexicographically smallest number.
solution:
1. State (r, sum), start (0,0); edge digit c -> ((10r+c)%d, sum+c) if sum+c <= s.
2. BFS, trying digits in increasing order; store parent and digit.
3. Fewer digits = smaller number; within a BFS layer queue order equals lexicographic order, so first hit is the minimum.
4. Reconstruct digits back to (0,0); unreachable -> -1.
complexity: O(10 * d * s) time, O(d * s) space

brief: Array of n zeros, q operations (add x on [l,r]), n,q <= 1e4. List every y in 1..n that equals the array maximum for some subset of operations.
key_idea: y is achievable iff some position can reach exactly y using only operations covering it; do subset-sum with a bitset while DFSing a segment tree where each op sits in O(log n) nodes.
solution:
1. Insert each operation's x into the O(log n) segment tree nodes covering [l,r].
2. DFS from the root carrying bitset cur (cur[0]=1); at a node apply cur |= cur << x for its ops.
3. At each leaf OR cur into ans (using only ops that cover the point gives max exactly y if y <= n).
4. Output y in 1..n with ans[y].
complexity: O(q log n * n / 64) time, O(n log n / 64 + q log n) space

brief: Generated array a (n <= 1e7), k <= 5. b_i = sum_{j<=i} C(i-j+1, k) a_j mod 998244353; output XOR of b_i * i.
key_idea: Pascal's rule C(m+1,t) = C(m,t) + C(m,t-1) gives b_t[i] = b_t[i-1] + b_{t-1}[i-1] + C(1,t)*a_i, so keep k+1 running values.
solution:
1. b_0[i] = prefix sum of a (C(.,0)=1).
2. For t >= 1: b_t[i] = b_t[i-1] + b_{t-1}[i-1] + [t==1]*a_i, all mod p.
3. Update t from k down to 1 (so b_{t-1} is still the old value), then b_0.
4. res ^= b_k[i] * i (no mod; fits in long long). Generate a on the fly; O(k) memory.

brief: Koa crosses n sea cells; at time t depth at i is d_i + p[t mod 2k] where p rises 0..k then falls to 1. Each second she moves forward or waits; depth must stay <= l where she stands. Can she reach the island?
key_idea: Cells with d_i + k <= l are safe forever and reset the state to 'tide k, falling'; between them simulate greedily: while falling wait as needed (tide = min(tide-1, l-d_i)), while rising you must keep moving.
solution:
1. tide = k, down = true at the shore.
2. Safe cell (d+k <= l): reset tide=k, down=true.
3. If d_i > l -> No.
4. If down: tide = min(tide-1, l-d_i) (waiting earlier is free since water falls); if tide <= 0 set tide=0, down=false.
5. If rising: tide++; if tide > l-d_i -> No.
6. Finish -> Yes.

brief: Array with a_i <= min(n,100). Maximize med(sub) - min(sub) over subarrays (median = element at ceil((k+1)/2) after sorting).
key_idea: Fix threshold x: med >= x iff the +1/-1 transformed sum (>=x -> +1) is >= 0; for each i check whether some subarray containing i has sum >= 0 (Kadane left + right), then candidate x - a_i.
solution:
1. For x = 1..100: v_i = +1 if a_i >= x else -1.
2. L[i] = best sum of subarray ending at i, R[i] = best starting at i (Kadane both ways).
3. If L[i] + R[i] - v_i >= 0, some subarray with med >= x contains a_i, so value >= x - a_i: ans = max(ans, x - a_i).
4. The optimum is hit with x = its median and i = its minimum.

brief: Count complete graphs on n vertices (n <= 250) with edge weights in [1,k] (k <= 250) where the total weight of edges at vertex 1 equals the MST weight, mod 998244353.
key_idea: The star at vertex 1 is an MST iff every other edge (u,v) has weight >= max(w(1,u), w(1,v)); assign star weights in increasing order and count the edges forced to be >= current weight.
solution:
1. dp[j] = ways with j of the n-1 other vertices assigned star weight <= w (and all edges among them fixed).
2. For weight w, add t new vertices: choose C(n-1-j, t); edges from them to the j old vertices and among themselves: e = t*j + t(t-1)/2, each has (k-w+1) choices.
3. nd[j+t] += dp[j] * C * (k-w+1)^e (precompute powers per w).
4. Answer dp[n-1] after w = k.
complexity: O(k * n^2) time (+ power tables), O(n^2) space

brief: Strip with n traffic lights at p_i, red at seconds l*k + d_i. You start at a_i at time 0 facing right; each second reverse on red, then move one cell. For q starts decide whether you eventually leave the strip.
key_idea: Moving right, (t - pos) mod k is invariant; moving left, (t + pos) mod k is; so 'bounce at light i' has a unique next bounce found by a hash map, giving a functional graph on 2n states where you escape iff the chain ends.
solution:
1. A_i = (d_i + p_i) mod k, B_i = (d_i - p_i) mod k.
2. After bouncing at i to go left, next bounce is the nearest j < i with A_j = A_i (then you go right); after bouncing to go right, the nearest j > i with B_j = B_i.
3. Build nxt for 2n states with a map while scanning; mark escape/loop by walking chains with colors (on-path = cycle).
4. Query a: key (-a) mod k; first light with p_j >= a and B_j = key (binary search in that key's list); none -> YES, else answer of state 'left from j'.
complexity: O((n + q) log n) time, O(n) space

brief: n <= 1000 trees, nest i has c_i birds (sum c <= 1e4) costing cost_i mana each; every bird raises capacity by B; moving to the next tree restores X mana up to capacity. Start with W mana/capacity. Maximize birds summoned.
key_idea: Swap value and state: dp[j] = maximum mana left after summoning j birds total (capacity is then W + B*j).
solution:
1. dp[0] = W, others -1 (impossible).
2. At tree i: nd[j+t] = max(dp[j] - t*cost_i) for t = 0..c_i while mana stays >= 0.
3. Move: nd[j] = min(nd[j] + X, W + B*j).
4. Answer = largest j with dp[j] >= 0. Total work <= (sum c)^2.
complexity: O((sum c)^2) time worst case, O(sum c) space

brief: k starts at 0; n <= 200 steps, step i lets you apply k = ceil(k + x_i) (type 1) or k = ceil(k * x_i) (type 2) between 0 and y_i times. For each j in 1..m (m <= 1e5) print the earliest step where k = j is possible.
key_idea: BFS by step: from every value reached before step i apply the operation up to y_i times, stopping as soon as a value is already reached (it is either an old start with full budget or reached with more budget left).
solution:
1. vis[0] = 1. Use integers: type 1 add ceil(x'/1e5); type 2 k = ceil(k*x'/1e5) = (k*x' + 99999)/100000.
2. For step i, collect current reachable values, process them from largest to smallest.
3. From s: repeat up to y times cur = f(cur); stop if cur > m or vis[cur]; else vis[cur]=1, ans[cur]=i.
4. Since f(x) > x and increasing, a smaller start reaching the same value has used more applications, so stopping is safe; each value is visited once per step -> O(nm).

brief: Tree with n <= 2000 vertices: find the minimum number of query vertices such that the vector of distances to a hidden vertex x always identifies x.
key_idea: Root at a vertex of degree >= 3; at every vertex, all but at most one child subtree must contain a query, and greedily f(v) = sum f(c) + max(0, #children with f(c)=0 - 1).
solution:
1. n = 1 -> 0. If no vertex has degree >= 3 (a path) -> 1.
2. Root at any vertex with degree >= 3 (the root itself never needs a query then).
3. DFS: f(v) = sum of f(children) + max(0, zeroChildren - 1).
4. Answer f(root).
complexity: O(n) time per test, O(n) space

brief: n monsters with health h_i. Use 1-MP single-damage spells, then one explosion of power x on monster i; a killed monster explodes for (health-1) on its neighbours, chaining. Minimize total MP to kill everyone.
key_idea: With target i (pay x = h_i), the kept healths must form a strictly decreasing chain outward: c_j = min(h_j, c_{j+1}-1); maximize the kept sum per side with a monotonic stack on h_j - j.
solution:
1. Cost for target i = sum(h) - (kept sum) + h_i, kept sum = L[i] + R[i] - h_i.
2. L[i]: pop stack while h_k - k > h_i - i; j = top (h_j - j <= h_i - i, so j keeps full h_j).
3. len = i - j; if len > h_i the chain hits 0 first: L[i] = h_i(h_i+1)/2; else L[i] = L[j] + sum of h_i, h_i-1, ..., h_i-len+1.
4. R[i] the same on the reversed array.
5. Answer min over i. Use long long.

brief: Deck of n suits x m ranks (m even) split evenly between two players. Suit 1 beats other suits; same suit higher rank beats lower. Count splits where player 1 can match each of player 2's cards with a beating card, mod 998244353.
key_idea: Each non-trump suit is a bracket sequence where player 2 may end with surplus e (to be beaten by trumps); trump suit is a bracket sequence where player 1 ends with surplus E = total of those surpluses.
solution:
1. w[e] = number of length-m +/-1 paths that never go negative and end at e (ballot numbers via O(m^2) DP).
2. In suit s != 1 scan ranks from low to high: player 2's card opens, player 1's card closes (must match an earlier lower card, so never negative); final balance e = player 2's unmatched cards, count w[e].
3. dp over suits 2..n: dp[a+e] += dp[a]*w[e] (total surplus <= m).
4. Answer = sum_E dp[E] * w[E] (trump suit, scanned the same way with roles swapped, leaves player 1 exactly E spare trumps).

brief: Start with [0,1]; repeatedly insert k = current inversion count anywhere. Count distinct arrays of length n (n <= 1e6) mod 998244353.
key_idea: Once k exceeds every element, inserting k anywhere but the end creates a new k' > all elements; so d[i] = i * sum_{j>i} d[j] + 1, and the early phase (k <= 1) contributes n-1 arrays plus ((m-2)(m-1)/2 - 1) ways to enter the big phase at length m.
solution:
1. Big phase: d[i] = i * (suffix sum of d over j > i) + 1 (the +1 = keep inserting at the end until length n).
2. Small phase: arrays of form 0,..,0,1,..: n-1 of them stay small to the end.
3. Entering the big phase at length m (first insertion of a 1 before some 1... ) can be done in (m-2)(m-1)/2 - 1 ways.
4. Answer = (n-1) + sum_{m=3..n} ((m-2)(m-1)/2 - 1) * d[m], computed backwards with a running suffix sum.
complexity: O(n) time per test, O(1) extra space

brief: Given bracket strings s and t (length <= 200, not necessarily regular), output a shortest regular bracket sequence containing both as subsequences.
key_idea: BFS over states (i, j, balance): appending a character advances each string whose next char matches; unit edges, so BFS gives the shortest, reconstruct via parents.
solution:
1. State (i, j, b) with 0 <= b <= ~200 (larger balance is never needed).
2. From a state append '(' (b+1) or ')' (b-1 >= 0); i advances if s[i] equals it, same for j.
3. BFS from (0,0,0) until (n, m, 0).
4. Store the appended char; walk back finding the predecessor with dist-1 that maps to the current state; reverse.
complexity: O(n * m * B) time and space (~8e6 states)

brief: Count bitonic permutations of 1..n (strictly up to a peak at 2..n-1, then down) with B_i = x and B_j = y, mod 1e9+7 (n <= 100).
key_idea: Build the permutation by placing values 1..n-1 in increasing order, each at the leftmost or rightmost free slot; value n fills the last slot, which must not be an end.
solution:
1. dp[l] = ways with l values placed on the left (v-1-l on the right).
2. Value v goes to slot l+1 (left) or n-(v-1-l) (right).
3. A placement is allowed iff (pos==i) == (v==x) and (pos==j) == (v==y).
4. Finally n goes to slot l+1, which must lie in [2, n-1] and satisfy the same check; sum dp[l].

brief: Tree (n <= 5e5); Cyndaquil starts at non-leaf v and wants to reach a leaf. Snorlax moves first and may block one edge at a time; after choosing a new edge he must wait k of Cyndaquil's turns (cooldown) before choosing another, but may also wait longer. Decide if Cyndaquil can surely reach a leaf.
key_idea: Not fully solved here. Necessary intuition: Cyndaquil needs a position where two different branches offer a leaf (or another winning spot) within k moves, but Snorlax can delay blocking until Cyndaquil commits, so the simple 'two leaves within k in different branches of v' test is NOT sufficient.
solution:
1. Exact (small n only): retrograde game analysis on states (turn, position, blocked edge, cooldown 0..k); Cyndaquil-turn states win if some move wins, Snorlax-turn states win if all options (keep, or new edge when cooldown <= 0) win.
2. Checked hypotheses with that solver: 'v has leaves within distance k in two different branches' and a fixpoint version both disagree on small random trees (e.g. path 4-0-1-2-3, k=2, v=1 is NO because Snorlax waits until Cyndaquil steps toward one end).
3. The intended O(n) characterization was not derived; treat this note as incomplete.
4. Sample checks of the simple test: cases 1,3,6 YES and 2,4,5 NO match, but it is wrong in general.
complexity: Exact brute force: O(n^2 k) states; intended solution unknown here

brief: Strip of m = n unit cells, initially color 0. For i = 1..n, paint a segment that is currently one color with color i. Given the final coloring (a permutation), count painting processes mod 998244353 (n <= 500).
key_idea: In a segment whose colors all exceed the current background, the smallest color c (at position p) is painted first over an interval [a,b] containing p; left and right parts become independent subproblems.
solution:
1. f(l,r) = ways to produce c[l..r] on a single-colored background; f(empty)=1.
2. p = position of the minimum color in [l,r].
3. A = sum over a in [l,p] of f(l,a-1) * f(a,p-1); B = sum over b in [p,r] of f(p+1,b) * f(b+1,r).
4. f(l,r) = A * B mod p; answer f(1,n). Memoize.

brief: Choose X <= m (m <= 1e15); a tower is built greedily by repeatedly adding the largest cube that keeps the volume <= X. Maximize the number of cubes, then X.
key_idea: For remaining limit m with a = floor(cbrt(m)), only two first choices matter: take a^3 (limit m - a^3) or take (a-1)^3 with limit a^3 - 1 - (a-1)^3.
solution:
1. rec(m, cnt, used): if m == 0 record (cnt, used).
2. a = integer cube root of m (fix floating error with while loops).
3. Branch 1: rec(m - a^3, cnt+1, used + a^3).
4. Branch 2 (a > 1): rec(a^3 - 1 - (a-1)^3, cnt+1, used + (a-1)^3).
5. Keep the lexicographically largest (cnt, used); depth is small (limits shrink fast).
complexity: About O(m^(1/3)) branching overall in practice (tiny), O(depth) stack

Other branch 8 with limit 26-8=18 gives 9 blocks with X=23.

brief: Given a_1..a_n, count permutations p where for each i the prefix p_1..p_i contains exactly a_i values <= i, mod 998244353.
key_idea: View p as rooks on an n x n board; a_i = rooks in the top-left i x i square, and going from i-1 to i adds row i and column i; free rows = free columns = (i-1) - a_{i-1}.
solution:
1. If a_n != n -> 0.
2. For each i: d = a_i - a_{i-1}, fr = (i-1) - a_{i-1}; if d not in {0,1,2} or fr < 0 -> 0.
3. d = 0: factor 1 (no rook in the new L-strip).
4. d = 1: rook in new row (fr columns), new column (fr rows) or corner (i,i): 2*fr + 1.
5. d = 2: one in row i and one in column i: fr^2. Multiply all factors.

brief: q <= 1e5 queries (b, l, r) with 2 <= b <= 10, r <= 1e18: count numbers in [l,r] whose base-b representation has every digit 0..b-1 occurring an even number of times.
key_idea: Precompute W[b][len][mask] = number of length-len digit strings whose digit-parity mask is mask; answer each query by a standard tight-prefix digit walk.
solution:
1. W[b][0][0] = 1; W[b][len][m] = sum over digit x of W[b][len-1][m ^ (1<<x)].
2. cnt(N): digits of N in base b, length L.
3. Shorter numbers: for len < L and leading digit f >= 1 add W[b][len-1][1<<f].
4. Same length: walk digits keeping mask of the tight prefix; for each smaller digit x (x >= 1 at the first position) add W[b][remaining][mask ^ (1<<x)]; at the end add 1 if mask == 0.
5. Answer cnt(r) - cnt(l-1).
complexity: O(sum_b b*60*2^b) precompute, O(60*b) per query
dry_run:
Query b=2, [4,9]: cnt(9) - cnt(3).
Magic numbers <= 9 in base 2: 3 (11), 9 (1001), 10? no -> cnt(9)=2? 3=11 and 9=1001 -> 2; cnt(3)=1.
Answer 2 - 1 = 1 (matches).

brief: q <= 1e5 operations: insert u into a set, or query (x,k,s): among v with k | gcd(x,v) and x+v <= s, output the v maximizing x XOR v (or -1). Values <= 1e5.
key_idea: Keep a binary trie for every k containing the inserted multiples of k, storing the minimum value in each subtree; query trie k greedily for max XOR among values <= s-x.
solution:
1. Precompute divisors of all numbers up to 1e5.
2. Insert u (skip duplicates) into the trie of each divisor d of u; each node stores min value in its subtree.
3. Query: if x % k != 0 or trie k is empty or its min > s-x -> -1.
4. Walk 17 bits from the top: prefer the child with bit opposite to x if its min <= s-x, else the other child (guaranteed valid).
5. The leaf path is v.
complexity: O(sum of divisors * 17) time and memory (~2e7 nodes worst case), O(17) per query
dry_run:
Sample 1: set {1,2}, trie k=1 holds both.
Query x=1, s=3: lim 2; bit1: want 1 -> node with min 2 <= 2 -> v=2.
Query s=2: lim 1 -> only 1 fits -> v=1; s=1: lim 0 -> -1. Output 2 1 -1 (matches).

brief: Given p <= 2e5, find the minimum number of nodes of a directed graph with exactly p mutually reachable unordered pairs, and the maximum number of one-way reachable pairs for that node count.
key_idea: Mutual pairs come from SCCs: p = sum C(s_i, 2); minimize sum s_i with an unbounded knapsack, then chain the SCCs so all other C(n,2) - p pairs are one-way.
solution:
1. dp[0] = 0; dp[i] = min over s >= 2 with C(s,2) <= i of dp[i - C(s,2)] + s.
2. n = dp[p] (singleton SCCs are useless for minimality).
3. Put SCCs in a line (edges forward): every pair in different SCCs is one-way: C(n,2) - p.
4. Print n and n(n-1)/2 - p.
dry_run:
p=4: options 3 (s=3 -> 3 pairs) + 1 (s=2) -> 5 nodes; or two... 4 = C(3,2)+C(2,2) best.
n=5, one-way pairs = 10 - 4 = 6.
Output 5 6 (matches); p=3 -> 3 0.

brief: Color some non-adjacent elements red; score = max red + min red + number of red. Maximize (n <= 2e5).
key_idea: Some optimal solution contains a global maximum M; sweep the minimum threshold downward activating elements, and with DSU segments count sum ceil(len/2), minus 1 if no segment can include an M while taking ceil(len/2).
solution:
1. Sort indices by value descending; activate them one by one (whole groups of equal values).
2. DSU over active consecutive runs: store start, length, and whether it contains an M at even/odd absolute index.
3. Segment is 'good' if even length and has any M, or odd length and has an M at the start's parity.
4. After activating all values >= v: cnt = sum ceil(len/2); score = M + v + cnt - (no good segment ? 1 : 0).
5. Answer is the maximum over thresholds.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
dry_run:
Sample 2: 4 5 4, M=5.
Threshold 5: segment [1], good, cnt 1 -> 5+5+1 = 11.
Threshold 4: segment [0..2] odd, M at index 1 (wrong parity) -> cnt 2-1 = 1 -> 5+4+1 = 10.
Answer 11 (matches). Verified vs brute force.

brief: n <= 20 piles with 1..m stones (m <= 2); some indices are good (1 always). Players alternately remove a pile at a good index <= current count (Alice first) until one pile remains; Alice maximizes, Bob minimizes its size. Sum the result over all m^n configurations mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: With m=2 a configuration is a bitmask; win[L][mask] = whether the final pile is 2 from a length-L sequence, computed for all lengths (who moves depends only on L).
solution:
1. m = 1 -> answer 1.
2. win[1][mask] = mask (pile with 2 stones).
3. For L = 2..n, mover is Alice iff (n-L) even. For each good c <= L remove bit c-1 (low | high << i).
4. Alice: win = any child wins; Bob: win = all children win.
5. Answer = 2^n + #masks with win[n][mask] = 1.
dry_run:
Test 3: n=3, good {1,2}.
Count of 3-bit masks where Alice (moves at L=3) can force a 2 after Bob's move at L=2: 3 masks.
Answer 8 + 3 = 11 (matches).

brief: Compress an n x m table to positive integers keeping the order and equalities inside every row and column, minimizing the maximum value; print the table.
key_idea: Union equal values in the same row/column with DSU, then process cells by increasing value: each component gets 1 + max of current row/column maxima of its cells.
solution:
1. For each row and column sort cells; union neighbours with equal values.
2. Sort all cells by value; process equal-value groups together.
3. For a group: component value = max over its cells of max(rowMx[r], colMx[c]) + 1.
4. Assign, then update rowMx and colMx with the new values.
5. Print results.
dry_run:
Sample 1: 1 2 / 3 4.
Value 1 -> 1; value 2 (row 0 max 1) -> 2; value 3 (col 0 max 1) -> 2; value 4 (row max 2, col max 2) -> 3.
Output 1 2 / 2 3 (matches).

brief: Tree with n <= 100 vertices: count k-subsets of vertices (k >= 2) whose pairwise distances are all equal, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: For k >= 3 all chosen vertices are at the same depth d from a common center, each in a different neighbour branch; count by a 'choose one from k distinct branches' knapsack per (center, depth).
solution:
1. k = 2: every pair works -> C(n,2).
2. For each center c, DFS each neighbour branch and count vertices at each depth d.
3. For each depth d: dp[j] = ways to pick j branches with one vertex each: dp[j] += dp[j-1] * cnt_branch[d] (j descending).
4. Add dp[k] to the answer over all centers and depths.
complexity: O(n^2 * k) per center sweep -> O(n^3) worst, O(n) space per branch
dry_run:
Test 3: edges 1-2, 2-3, 2-4, 4-5, k=3.
Center 2, depth 1: branches {1},{3},{4} each 1 vertex -> C(3,3) = 1.
Other centers/depths give 0. Answer 1 (matches).

brief: A tree is good if it is the intersection graph of some set of segments. Given a tree (n <= 3e5), find the largest good connected subtree.
key_idea: Segment intersection trees are caterpillars: a spine path plus leaves attached; size = sum over spine of (deg-1) + 2, so find the max-weight path with weight deg(v)-1.
solution:
1. val(v) = deg(v) - 1 (using degrees in the whole tree: all neighbours of a spine vertex can be included).
2. Root the tree; down[v] = val(v) + max child down.
3. best = max over v of val(v) + top two child down values.
4. Answer best + 2 (the two spine ends' outer neighbours). Use BFS order to avoid recursion.
dry_run:
Sample: vertex 1 and 2,3,4 have degree 3 -> val 2; leaves val 0.
Best path 2-1-3: 2+2+2 = 6.
Answer 6 + 2 = 8 (matches).

brief: Same as 1811G1 (count maximum-length nice paths: blocks of k same-colored tiles) but n <= 5000 with sum n^2 <= 2.5e7, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Same O(n^2) DP as G1 (last block ends at i, previous block ends at j, choose k-1 of the 'same' tiles between), but binomials from factorials instead of a table.
solution:
1. Precompute factorials and inverse factorials up to 5000.
2. len[0]=0, cnt[0]=1 (empty path).
3. For each i scan j = i-1 down to 0, same = #tiles of color c_i in (j, i); if same >= k-1: candidate len[j]+1 with cnt[j]*C(same, k-1).
4. Keep the max length and sum counts on ties; answer sums cnt over states of max length.

brief: Count n-digit numbers x (n <= 1000, no leading zeros) having a suffix that is the decimal form of a positive y divisible by k (k <= 100), modulo m.
key_idea: Build x from the last digit; dp[r] = suffixes with value mod k = r that contain no valid y yet; the first time a nonzero digit makes the remainder 0, all remaining higher digits are free.
solution:
1. dp[0] = 1 (empty suffix); p10 = 10^i mod k.
2. Position i from the right: digit d (1..9 at the top position, else 0..9); nr = (r + d*p10) % k.
3. If d != 0 and nr == 0: a valid y exists -> add dp[r] * (ways to fill the rest: 9*10^(rest-1), or 1 at the top) to the answer.
4. Otherwise nd[nr] += dp[r]. Everything mod m.
dry_run:
n=1, k=2: top digit d in 1..9, nr = d % 2.
d = 2,4,6,8 give nr = 0 -> 4 numbers.
Answer 4 (matches); n=2 gives 45 (matches).

brief: 7x7 black/white grid: minimum cell flips so that no black cell has all four diagonal neighbours black (t <= 200).
key_idea: An X only involves cells of one (i+j) parity, so the two parity classes are independent; for each, iterative-deepening search: find a violating X and try whitening each of its 5 cells.
solution:
1. For parity p in {0,1}, find the minimum d such that dfs(d) succeeds.
2. dfs(d): find any black center (i+j)%2 == p with 4 black diagonals; none -> true; d == 0 -> false.
3. Try setting each of the 5 cells to white, recurse with d-1, restore.
4. Only black->white flips are useful. Answer = sum over both parities (each needs at most 4).
complexity: O(5^d * 25) per class with d <= 4, tiny
dry_run:
Test 2: black block rows 2-4, cols 1-5 (0-based) gives X centres (3,2),(3,4) of one parity and (3,3) of the other.
Centres (3,2),(3,4) share corners (2,3),(4,3): whitening (2,3) kills both -> 1 flip.
(3,3) needs 1 flip. Total 2 (matches).

brief: n x m grid (<= 2000) with rocks; walk from (1,1) to (n,m) moving right/down; stepping on a rock pushes the whole rock chain forward, illegal if anything leaves the grid. Count legal paths mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Split paths into maximal straight runs: A[i][j] = ways arriving moving down (next run goes right), B[i][j] = arriving moving right; a run right from (i,j) can reach column m-1-(rocks in row i after j), so add to a range with difference arrays.
solution:
1. Suffix rock counts per row (rr) and per column (rd).
2. A[0][0] = B[0][0] = 1 (special case n=m=1 -> 1).
3. From A[i][j] (turn right): columns j+1 .. m-1-rr[i][j+1] get += A[i][j] in B (row difference array).
4. From B[i][j] (turn down): rows i+1 .. n-1-rd[i+1][j] get += B[i][j] in A (column difference array).
5. Answer A[n-1][m-1] + B[n-1][m-1].
dry_run:
Sample 2: 2x3, rock at (2,3) = goal cell.
Any run into the goal pushes the rock out of the grid: limits stop at column 1 / row 0.
Answer 0 (matches); sample 3 gives 4. Verified vs brute force on small grids.

brief: Array of length n with some -1 entries; fill them with 1..k so no odd-length (>1) palindromic subarray exists. Count fillings mod 998244353.
key_idea: An odd palindrome exists iff a[i] == a[i+2] for some i, so split into even/odd positions and count sequences with no two adjacent equal; each gap of L blanks between fixed values depends only on whether the ends are equal.
solution:
1. Split into even-index and odd-index subsequences; answer = product.
2. Fixed adjacent equal values -> 0.
3. same[L], diff[L] = ways to fill L blanks between equal / different fixed ends: same[0]=0, diff[0]=1; same[L] = (k-1)*diff[L-1]; diff[L] = same[L-1] + (k-2)*diff[L-1].
4. Blanks before the first / after the last fixed value: (k-1)^len each; all blank: k*(k-1)^(len-1).
dry_run:
Sample 3: 1 -1 -1 1 2, k=3.
Even positions: 1, -1, 2 -> diff[1] = same[0] + 1*diff[0] = 1.
Odd positions: -1, 1 -> (k-1)^1 = 2.
Answer 2 (matches).

brief: Move from (0,0) to (n,m) (n*m <= 1e4): each second go down, right or stay. r <= 100 railgun shots each hit a whole row or column at the end of a given second. Earliest safe arrival time or -1.
key_idea: Time-layered reachability: you never need more than n+m+r seconds (each shot costs at most one wait), so propagate the reachable set second by second and clear shot lines.
solution:
1. cur = {(0,0)} at t=0.
2. For t = 1 .. n+m+r: nx = cur (stay) plus down/right moves from cur.
3. Clear every cell on rows/columns shot at second t.
4. If (n,m) is in nx, answer t; otherwise continue. Never reached -> -1.
dry_run:
Test 1: 1x3, shots t1 col0, t2 col1, t3 col2, t4 row1.
t1: (0,1); t2: (0,2); t3: (0,3); t4: (1,3) hit -> wait at (0,3).
t5: (1,3) reached -> 5 (matches full sample: 5 -1 3 6 10).

brief: Strings s (<= 2000) and p (<= 500): for each x in 0..|s|, delete exactly x characters to maximize the number of non-overlapping occurrences of p in the result.
key_idea: dp[i][j] = max occurrences using s[0..i) with j deletions; a match starting at i uses the shortest window containing p as a subsequence and deletes the extra characters inside it.
solution:
1. For each i greedily match p from i; window end e and cost d = (e - i) - |p| (or none).
2. Transitions from dp[i][j]: keep s[i] -> dp[i+1][j]; delete s[i] -> dp[i+1][j+1]; take match -> dp[e][j+d] = max(.., dp[i][j]+1).
3. Output dp[n][x] for x = 0..n.
dry_run:
s=axbaxxb, p=ab: window at 0 is 'axb' (d=1), at 3 'axxb' (d=2).
Taking both: 3 deletions -> 2 occurrences.
Output 0 1 1 2 1 1 0 0 (matches).

brief: Insert exactly k pluses between n digits (n <= 1e5, no two adjacent, not at ends) and sum the values of all resulting expressions mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Digit i contributes d*10^l when the next plus is l digits after it: C(n-2-l, k-1) placements; if it is in the last number, d*10^(n-1-i)*C(i, k).
solution:
1. Precompute factorials, powers of 10.
2. S[x] = sum_{l=0..x} 10^l * C(n-2-l, k-1) (prefix sums).
3. For digit i: weight = S[n-2-i] (a plus closes its number) + 10^(n-1-i) * C(i, k) (no plus after it).
4. Answer = sum of digit * weight mod p.

brief: Connected multigraph (n <= 500, m <= 2.5e5) with weighted wires. A spell on wire (u,v) detaches it from v and reattaches it as (u,t) for any neighbour t of v, costing w_i. Minimize total spell cost plus travel time from 1 to n.
key_idea: Use a single edge of weight w for everything: each spell or traversal costs w, so answer = min over edges of w * (minimum number of moves to make it join 1 and n, plus 1 traversal), with moves counted by unweighted hop distances (Floyd).
solution:
1. Floyd-Warshall on hop counts d (every edge = 1).
2. For edge (u,v,w): option A: slide ends to 1 and n: d(1,u) + d(v,n) + 1 (or swapped).
3. Option B: move one end to some y (d(u,y) or d(v,y)), make a self-loop at y (+1), then stretch to 1 and n: + d(y,1) + d(y,n), + 1 traversal.
4. Answer = min over edges of w * best count. Use long long.
dry_run:
Test 2: edges all weight 1 except (1,3) weight 2; n=4.
Edge (2,4,1): d(1,2)=1, d(4,4)=0 -> 1+0+1 = 2 moves -> cost 2.
Answer 2 (matches); test 1 -> 9, test 3 -> 154 (match).

brief: f(w) = number of permutations of 0..n-1 where MEX i is achieved by some subarray iff w_i = 1. Given s over {0,1,?} and c, choose ? to minimize f(w) not divisible by c; print it mod 1e9+7 or -1.
key_idea: Removing the largest value keeps all smaller conditions, and MEX i is achievable iff value i lies outside the span of 0..i-1, i.e. at an end of the length-(i+1) array: f(w) = prod_{i=1}^{n-1} (w_i ? 2 : i-1), needing w_1 = w_n = 1.
solution:
1. If c = 1, or s_1 = '0' or s_n = '0' -> -1 (f = 0 is divisible by c).
2. Cheapest: '?' at i=2 -> factor 1, at i >= 3 -> factor 2.
3. Write c = 2^e * c'. Base is divisible iff v2(base) >= e and c' divides its odd part (compute mod c').
4. Since factors only get larger, the only fix is to drop the 2-adic valuation below e: switch r = v2 - e + 1 '?' at even i >= 4 (factor i-1 odd) choosing the smallest i; not enough -> -1.
5. Output the product mod 1e9+7.
complexity: O(n) time per test, O(n) space
dry_run:
Test 7: n=5, c=8, s=100?1.
Factors: i1=2, i2=1, i3=2, i4 '?'=2 -> base 8, divisible by 8 (e=3, v2=3).
r=1: switch i=4 -> factor 3: 2*1*2*3 = 12.
Answer 12 (matches; all 10 samples match).

brief: Build an array by adding numbers to either end; equal adjacent elements merge into their sum repeatedly. Given target a (adjacent distinct) and k, can exactly k additions produce a?
key_idea: Any count between n and the maximum works; max for x = o*2^p alone is 2^p pieces, but next to a neighbour y with the same odd part and y < x the touching block must skip y: 1 + (x - 2y)/o. Try every starting element.
solution:
1. full(x) = x / oddpart(x).
2. nextTo(x, y) = 1 + (x - 2y)/o if oddpart(y) == o and y < x, else x/o.
3. Starting at s: elements left of s are built next to their right neighbour, right of s next to their left neighbour; prefix/suffix sums give total(s).
4. YES iff k <= max_s total(s) (k >= n is given).
complexity: O(n log A) time, O(n) space
dry_run:
Test 2: [2,1,4], k=7.
s=0: 2 + nextTo(1,2)=1 + nextTo(4,1)=1+(4-2)/1=3 -> 6.
s=1: 1+1+3 = 5; s=2: 4+1+1 = 6. Max 6 < 7 -> NO (matches). Brute-force checked on small arrays.

brief: n <= 2000 questions with k options and answers h. A suit a is shifted cyclically by one. Count suits whose shifted score is strictly greater than the original score, mod 998244353.
key_idea: Only positions with h_i != h_{i+1} matter: each gives +1, -1 (one way each) or 0 (k-2 ways); by symmetry #positive = (k^m - #zero)/2.
solution:
1. m = #i with h_i != h_{(i+1) mod n}; if m = 0 answer 0.
2. zero = sum_j C(m,j) * C(m-j,j) * (k-2)^(m-2j) (j pluses, j minuses).
3. positive = (k^m - zero) / 2 mod p.
4. Multiply by k^(n-m) for the irrelevant positions.
complexity: O(m^2) for binomials (or O(m) with factorials), O(m^2) space

brief: f(t) = max number of pieces when splitting t into consecutive pieces that are each a prefix of t. For q <= 100 queries (l, r) on s (n <= 1e6) output sum_{j=l..r} f(s[l..j]).
key_idea: For u = s[l..], dp[len] = 1 + dp[a] for the largest a < len with z[a] >= len - a (the shortest valid last piece), else 1; a stack of candidates gives O(len) per query.
solution:
1. For each query build u = s[l..r] and its Z-array.
2. Sweep len = 1..m: push candidate a = len-1 (if >= 1).
3. Pop while top + z[top] < len (dead forever since len grows).
4. dp[len] = top exists ? dp[top] + 1 : 1; add to the sum.
5. Greedy 'largest a' was verified against the full DP on random strings.

brief: Online tree (Q <= 4e5): add node with weight W under R, or query the longest sequence starting at R going to ancestors where each next node is the nearest ancestor with weight >= current, total weight <= X. Inputs XOR-decoded with last answer.
key_idea: Each node's next element is fixed when it is added: the nearest ancestor with weight >= W, found by binary lifting on R's already-built 'next' chain (weights along it are non-decreasing); store 2^j jumps and weight sums.
solution:
1. Sentinel node 0 with infinite weight; up[v][j], sm[v][j] = node and weight sum after 2^j chain steps.
2. Add v under R: if w[R] >= W next = R, else climb R's chain with lifting while weight < W, then one more step.
3. Fill up[v][j] and sums (cap at INF).
4. Query: if w[R] > X answer 0; else take R, then greedily take 2^j jumps whose sum fits X.
5. Decode inputs with XOR of last answer.
complexity: O(Q log Q) time, O(Q log Q) space
dry_run:
Sample 1: add node 2 (w=1) under 1. Query R=2, X=0: w=1 > 0 -> 0.
Query R=2, X=1 -> 1. Add node 3 (w=1) under 2: next(3) = 2.
Query R=3, X=2 (decoded) -> take 3 then 2 -> 2. Output 0 1 1 2 (matches).

brief: Rooted tree; Chefir at v with k stamina: moving down is free, moving up costs 1. For each query (v,k) output the max distance from v to a reachable vertex.
key_idea: Go up j <= k steps to ancestor p then down its deepest branch not containing v: distance = dep[v] + (best descent from p avoiding the child towards v) - dep[p]; keep that value per child edge and take a max over the first k ancestors with binary lifting.
solution:
1. h[v] = height of subtree; per node keep best and second-best (1 + h(child)) and which child gives the best.
2. val[x] (x with parent p) = (best of p excluding x's branch, 0 if none) - dep[p].
3. Binary lifting: up[x][j], mx[x][j] = max val over the 2^j chain nodes starting at x.
4. Query: k = min(k, dep[v]); M = max of val over the k nodes v, par(v), ...; answer max(h[v], dep[v] + M).
complexity: O((n + q) log n) time, O(n log n) space
dry_run:
Test 1: path 1-2-3 with 3 having children 4,5. Query (5,1).
h[5]=0; climb 1 step: x=5, p=3, best excluding 5 = 1 (via 4), dep[3]=2 -> val = -1.
Answer max(0, dep[5]=3 + (-1)) = 2 (matches).

brief: Events: handle-change opportunities and visits by friends (m <= 40). A friend is happy if the handle is their name at all of their visits. Maximize happy friends.
key_idea: Two friends visiting within the same segment (between change points) conflict; answer = maximum independent set of the conflict graph on 40 vertices via meet in the middle.
solution:
1. Map names to ids; collect the set of friends in each segment and make them pairwise adjacent (bitmask adjacency).
2. Split vertices into halves A (h = m/2) and B.
3. bestB[mask] = max independent subset within mask of B: drop lowest v, or take it and remove its neighbours.
4. For each independent subset S of A: allowed B = B minus neighbours of S; ans = max |S| + bestB[allowed].
dry_run:
Sample 1: segments {motarack, mike}, {light}.
Conflict edge motarack-mike only.
MIS = {motarack, light} -> 2 (matches).

brief: Word w (n <= 1e5) and three religion strings (each <= 250) changed by q <= 1000 append/pop operations; after each, decide whether the three can be disjoint subsequences of w.
key_idea: dp[a][b][c] = shortest prefix of w that embeds the three prefixes disjointly, using a next-occurrence table; an append to string i only requires recomputing the layer with index = its new length (250^2 states).
solution:
1. nx[i][ch] = first position >= i holding ch (n if none).
2. step(pos, ch) = nx[pos][ch] + 1, or n+1 if impossible.
3. dp[a][b][c] = min over the last character coming from one of the three strings of step(previous state, that char).
4. On '+ i c': recompute only states whose i-th index equals the new length. On '-': just shrink.
5. Answer YES iff dp[len1][len2][len3] <= n.
dry_run:
Sample 1 after 6 changes: ad, bc, ab inside abdabc -> dp <= 6 -> YES.
Append c to religion 1 ('adc'): no disjoint embedding -> NO.
Pop from religion 2 -> YES (matches).

brief: DAG with all nodes blue; token game: Cry and River alternate moving along edges (Cry first); reaching a sink means Cry wins, reaching a red node means River wins. Queries: recolor a node red, or ask whether Cry wins starting from u.
key_idea: States (node, player to move) only ever flip from Cry-win to Cry-loss as nodes turn red, so propagate losses backwards once each: River state loses if any successor loses, Cry state loses when its count of winning successors hits 0.
solution:
1. win[v][0] (Cry to move) and win[v][1] (River to move) start true; cnt[v] = outdeg(v).
2. Turning u red: mark (u,0) and (u,1) losing and push them.
3. Pop (x, px); for each predecessor y (state (y, 1-px)): if it is a River state -> it loses; if a Cry state -> --cnt[y], at 0 it loses.
4. Query u: print win[u][0].
complexity: O(n + m + q) total time, O(n + m) space
dry_run:
Sample: red 3 and 4. (3,*),(4,*) lose.
(1, River) loses via 3; (2, River) loses via 3 -> Cry at 1: successors 2,3,4 all River-states lost -> (1, Cry) loses.
Query 1 -> NO; query 2 -> Cry moves to 5 (fine) -> YES (matches).

brief: n distinct names (total length <= 1e5); replace each by a non-empty prefix of itself so all new names are distinct. Minimize the total length.
key_idea: Build a trie; process nodes bottom-up keeping a max-heap of chosen depths in each subtree (small-to-large merge); at a node where no name ends, move the deepest chosen name up to this node.
solution:
1. Insert all names into a trie; mark word ends; depth = prefix length.
2. Process nodes in reverse BFS order; merge children's heaps into the largest one.
3. If a word ends at v: push dep[v].
4. Else if the heap is non-empty: pop the max and push dep[v] (shorten the longest name to this free prefix).
5. Answer = sum of the root heap.
complexity: O(L log^2 L) time, O(L) space (L = total length)

brief: Binary string s with q point flips; after each, output the sum over all non-empty subsequences of their number of runs, mod 998244353.
key_idea: runs = 1 + #adjacent differing pairs; positions i<j are adjacent in exactly 2^i * 2^(n-1-j) subsequences, so the answer = 2^n - 1 + sum over differing pairs, maintained with BITs of 2^i and 2^(n-1-j) per character.
solution:
1. BIT A[c] holds 2^i at positions with s_i = c; BIT B[c] holds 2^(n-1-i).
2. Initial S = sum over j of 2^(n-1-j) * A[other char](prefix < j).
3. Contribution of position p: 2^(n-1-p) * A[o](< p) + 2^p * B[o](> p), o = opposite char.
4. Flip p: S -= contribution, update BITs, flip, S += new contribution.
5. Print S + 2^n - 1.
complexity: O((n + q) log n) time, O(n) space
dry_run:

Answer 3 + 7 = 10 (matches); next flip -> 7.

brief: Tree with values a_i (possibly negative). Repeatedly delete leaves (possibly everything), then compress degree-2 vertices. Maximize the sum of remaining vertex values.
key_idea: After compression exactly the kept vertices with degree != 2 count; dp[v] = best when v is kept and connected to its parent, depending on whether v has 0, 1 (compressed) or >= 2 kept children (then all extra positive children are free gains).
solution:
1. Sort children dp values descending: c0 >= c1 >= ...
2. dp[v] = max(a_v [leaf], c0 [degree 2, compressed], a_v + c0 + c1 + sum of positive c_i, i >= 2 [degree >= 3]).
3. v as the top vertex: max(a_v, a_v + c0, c0 + c1 [compressed], a_v + c0 + c1 + c2 + positive rest).
4. Answer = max over v of the top case, and 0 (delete all).
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
dry_run:

Answer 3 (matches). Verified vs brute force.

brief: Complete graph on n cities; edges of a given spanning tree cost x, all others cost y. Find the cheapest Hamiltonian path.
key_idea: If x < y maximize tree edges used = maximum vertex-disjoint path cover of the tree (greedy: each vertex links up to 2 children that still have a free end); if x >= y avoid tree edges entirely unless the tree is a star.
solution:
1. x >= y: if some vertex has degree n-1 (star) answer (n-2)*y + x, else (n-1)*y.
2. x < y: process vertices bottom-up; take = min(2, #children with a free end); used += take; v has a free end iff take < 2.
3. Answer used*x + (n-1-used)*y. Use long long.

brief: For every non-empty subsequence of a (a_i < n), the score is the max total MEX over a partition into groups; sum scores mod 998244353.
key_idea: With value counts c_0, c_1, ..., the best score is sum_i min(c_0..c_i); count subsequences by DP over values with state m = current prefix minimum of chosen counts.
solution:
1. cnt[v] = occurrences of v.
2. dp for value 0: dp[j] = C(c0, j) for j >= 1 (m = 0 never contributes, drop it).
3. Value i: new[m] = dp[m] * (sum_{j>=m} C(c_i, j)) + C(c_i, m) * (sum_{m'>m} dp[m']) using suffix sums; sizes stay <= c_i + 1, so total O(n).
4. After value i add (sum_m m*dp[m]) * 2^(#elements with value > i).
5. Stop at the first value with zero count.
complexity: O(n) time per test (after factorials), O(n) space

brief: Two players start at scores a and b; for t turns each adds an integer in [-k,k]. Count the (2k+1)^(2t) games where the first player ends strictly higher, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Only the difference matters: it is a sum of 2t independent values in [-k,k] (negating the second player's choices), counted by a DP with prefix sums.
solution:
1. Offset the difference range [-2tk, 2tk].
2. Repeat 2t times: nd[i] = sum of dp[i-k .. i+k] using prefix sums.
3. Answer = sum of dp[D] over D with a + D > b.

brief: A sequence is almost increasing if min(b1,b2) <= min(b2,b3) <= ... Find the longest almost increasing subsequence (n <= 5e5).
key_idea: Such a sequence is a non-decreasing chain of 'lows' with optionally one big element (>= the next low) before the first low and between consecutive lows; dp over lows with two BITs, using the first element >= a_j after j as the big one.
solution:
1. dp[i] = best length ending with low i.
2. Option A: dp[j]+1 for j<i, a_j <= a_i (BIT1 prefix max by value).
3. Option B: dp[j]+2 when some x between j and i is big; it suffices to insert j into BIT2 when the first element >= a_j after j appears (monotonic stack pops), since a smaller x would itself be a low.
4. Leading big: dp[i] >= 2 for i > 0.
5. Order per i: query, then pop stack into BIT2, push i, update BIT1. Answer max dp.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

brief: n <= 100 numbers; a move picks a prime power p^k dividing some number and replaces every number divisible by p^k with x/p^k. Normal play; who wins?
key_idea: Primes are independent games; for prime p the state is the set of exponents present (bitmask), a move k maps mask to (mask & low k-1 bits) | (mask >> k); Sprague-Grundy with memoization and XOR.
solution:
1. Factorize each number by trial division; for each prime p set bit e-1 for exponent e.
2. grundy(0)=0; grundy(mask) = mex over k = 1..highest exponent of grundy((mask & ((1<<(k-1))-1)) | (mask >> k)).
3. Memoize in a map (few states in practice).
4. XOR over primes: non-zero -> Mojtaba, else Arpa.
complexity: O(n sqrt(A)) factorization + small memoized search

brief: n x m grid of '.'/'#' (nm <= 1e6). Pick one row and one column and fill them with '#'. Maximize the largest connected component.
key_idea: The new component = filled cross + every old component touching it; a component with bounding box rows [r1,r2], cols [c1,c2] touches row r iff r in [r1-1, r2+1] (same for columns), so add its size with 1D and 2D difference arrays and subtract the doubly counted rectangle.
solution:
1. BFS components, recording size and bounding box.
2. R[r] += size for r in [r1-1, r2+1]; C[c] += size for c in [c1-1, c2+1]; RC[r][c] += size on the rectangle (2D difference).
3. Prefix-sum all three.
4. For each (r,c): value = R[r] + C[c] - RC[r][c] + dots(row r) + dots(col c) - [cell (r,c) is '.'].
5. Answer the maximum.

brief: Graph (n,m <= 1e4); f friends at vertex 1 go home; k <= 6 have no car. A driver can drop carless friends whose homes lie on one shortest path to its home. Minimize the number of carless friends who walk.
key_idea: BFS layers; for each vertex keep the set of collectable masks (a 64-bit bitset over the 2^k masks) along shortest paths; then a subset-union knapsack over drivers.
solution:
1. BFS from 1; own[v] = mask of carless friends living at v.
2. In BFS order: reach[v] = { m | own[v] : m in reach[u], u a predecessor with d[u] = d[v]-1 } (bitset over 64 masks).
3. dp = {0}; for each driver i: dp = dp U { a | b : a in dp, b in reach[h_i] }.
4. Answer = k - max popcount of a mask in dp.
complexity: O((n + m) * 2^k + f * 4^k) time, O(n) space

brief: For each of n <= 600 opening brackets (left to right) the distance to its matching closing bracket must lie in [l_i, r_i]. Output any correct bracket sequence of length 2n satisfying this, or IMPOSSIBLE.
key_idea: Closing the innermost open bracket as early as allowed never hurts: at each position close the stack top if its distance >= l, else open the next bracket; fail if a top overshoots r or nothing remains to open.
solution:
1. Stack of (open position, index).
2. At position pos: if top exists and pos - open >= l[top]: if also > r[top] -> IMPOSSIBLE, else write ')' and pop.
3. Otherwise open the next bracket (if none left -> IMPOSSIBLE) after checking the top has not already exceeded r.
4. At the end the stack must be empty.

brief: Array a and strictly decreasing b (n*m <= 3e5); k starts at 1. Free op: k++ (k < m); paid op: remove a prefix with sum <= b_k for cost m-k. Find the minimum cost to empty a and the number of optimal operation sequences mod 1e9+7, or -1.
key_idea: dp[i][k] = (min cost, ways) to delete a[i..] at level k: either k -> k+1 or remove a[i..j) for any j up to the two-pointer bound R_k(i); a (min, count) segment tree over j answers the range.
solution:
1. Process k = m down to 1, keeping column k+1.
2. dp[n][k] = (0,1). For i = n-1..0: R = largest j with sum a[i..j) <= b_k (pointer moves left as i decreases).
3. Remove option: range (min,count) over dp[i+1..R][k] plus cost m-k.
4. Increase option (k < m): dp[i][k+1]. Combine: smaller cost wins, equal costs add counts.
5. Answer dp[0][1] or -1 if infinite.
complexity: O(n*m*log n) time, O(n) space per column

brief: Tree with n <= 6000 cities, populations r_i. Choose a simple path and concert cities on it with strictly increasing populations along the path; maximize the number of concerts.
key_idea: Every path is a root-to-node path for one of its endpoints as root; DFS from every root maintaining the patience-sorting LIS array with O(1) rollback.
solution:
1. For each root s, DFS.
2. Entering v: pos = lower_bound(tails, r_v); replace tails[pos] (remember old value) or append.
3. Update best with tails.size(); recurse to children; on exit restore tails.
4. Answer best over all roots.
complexity: O(n^2 log n) time (~2 s worst), O(n) space

brief: String of (,),[,] (n <= 1e6). Flipping a bracket's direction is free, turning square into round costs 1. For each query substring (even length) find the minimum cost to make it a correct bracket sequence.
key_idea: A square pair must match an opening at one parity with a closing at the other parity (even-length inside), so answer = |#square brackets at odd positions - #square at even positions| in the range.
solution:
1. pre[i] = prefix sum of +1 for square brackets at odd index, -1 at even index.
2. Query (l,r): print |pre[r] - pre[l-1]|.
3. Round brackets never cost anything (direction flips are free).

brief: n stickers; players alternately take the k >= 2 leftmost stickers, gain their sum and put back one sticker with that sum, until one sticker remains. Output Petya's score minus Gena's under optimal play.
key_idea: A move always takes a prefix ending at some j and gains pre[j]; f_i = best difference for the mover when the next take must end at index >= i: f_i = max(f_{i+1}, pre_i - f_{i+1}).
solution:
1. Prefix sums pre.
2. f_n = pre_n (take everything).
3. For i = n-1 down to 2: f = max(f, pre_i - f).
4. Answer f_2. Use long long.

brief: f(b) = min point changes so b has k consecutive values each one more than the previous. For queries (l,r) with r >= l+k-1 output sum_{j=l+k-1..r} f(a[l..j]).
key_idea: With b_i = a_i - i, the cost of window s is c_s = k - (max frequency of b in [s, s+k)); the query is a sum of prefix minima of c over [l, r-k+1], answered offline by sweeping l leftwards with range-assign / range-sum.
solution:
1. Sliding window over b with value counts and count-of-counts gives c_s for all windows.
2. Group queries by l; R = r-k+1.
3. Sweep l from right to left: positions s >= l store min(c[l..s]); new c[l] overwrites [l, next smaller index - 1] (monotonic stack) -> segment tree range assign.
4. Answer = range sum over [l, R].
complexity: O((n + q) log n) time, O(n) space

brief: Infinite tree where every node has n children with edge lengths d_i <= 100. Count nodes within distance x (x <= 1e9) of the root, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: dp[t] = sum_d cnt[d] * dp[t-d] is a linear recurrence of order 100; add the running sum S as an extra state and raise the 101 x 101 matrix to the x-th power.
solution:
1. cnt[d] = number of children edges of length d.
2. State (dp[t], dp[t-1], ..., dp[t-99], S[t]); dp[0] = S[0] = 1.
3. Transition row 0: cnt[1..100]; rows 1..99 shift; last row: S[t+1] = S[t] + new dp.
4. Answer = S[x] via fast matrix power.
complexity: O(101^3 log x) time, O(101^2) space

brief: n tasks with non-decreasing deadlines; m options (task e, time t, +p%) each usable once and executed sequentially. Output an order of options finishing every task (>= 100%) by its deadline, or -1.
key_idea: Do tasks in deadline order; for each task independently pick the minimum-time subset reaching 100% with a 0/1 knapsack capped at 100 percent, then check cumulative time.
solution:
1. Group options by task.
2. For task i: dp[j][p] = min time with first j options reaching p% (p capped at 100).
3. If dp[c][100] infinite or time + dp > a_i -> -1.
4. Reconstruct chosen options from the table, append, time += dp[c][100].
5. Print all chosen indices (task by task).
complexity: O(100 * m) time, O(100 * m) space

brief: Rooted tree with m leaves; leaves get numbers 1..m. Players alternately move a piece from the root down (first maximizes the final leaf number, second minimizes). Output the result when the numbers are arranged to maximize it, and when arranged to minimize it.
key_idea: Track how many of the best leaves the outcome needs: for the maximizing arrangement, a max-node needs min over children, a min-node needs the sum; answer = m - A(root) + 1. Symmetric for the minimizing arrangement: answer B(root).
solution:
1. Root at 1; depth parity decides who moves (even = maximizer).
2. Leaves: A = B = 1.
3. Even depth: A = min(A children), B = sum(B children).
4. Odd depth: A = sum(A children), B = min(B children).
5. Print m - A[1] + 1 and B[1].

brief: Count n-digit base-k tickets (n <= 100, k <= 30) where some digit equals the sum of the others mod k, modulo prime m.
key_idea: A digit d works iff 2d == S (mod k) with S the total sum; count the complement: for each target S, digit sequences avoiding all d with 2d == S and summing to S.
solution:
1. For S in 0..k-1: banned digits = {d : 2d % k == S}.
2. dp over n digits of sum mod k using only allowed digits; take dp[S].
3. Unlucky = sum over S; answer = k^n - unlucky mod m.
complexity: O(k * n * k^2) time, O(k) space

brief: Text of n <= 300 words. One abbreviation replaces at least two equal non-overlapping word segments by the uppercase first letters of their words. Minimize the text length.
key_idea: lcp[i][j] over words lets us check segment equality in O(1); for each segment (i, L) count greedy non-overlapping copies to the right; saving per copy = (letters + L - 1) - L.
solution:
1. total = sum of word lengths + n - 1.
2. lcp[i][j] = w[i]==w[j] ? lcp[i+1][j+1]+1 : 0.
3. For each start i and length L (letters = sum of lengths): scan j from i+L, if lcp[i][j] >= L count it and jump j += L, else j++.
4. If count >= 2: saving = count * (letters - 1).
5. Answer total - max saving.

brief: n <= 1000 cards with values 1..8. Find the longest subsequence where all 8 value counts differ by at most 1 and each value's cards are consecutive in the subsequence.
key_idea: Binary search the base count c (each value used c or c+1 times); for fixed c, dp[pos][mask] = max number of values taking c+1 copies, jumping to just after the c-th/(c+1)-th occurrence.
solution:
1. pos[v] = occurrence list; idx[i] = rank of i in its list.
2. check(c): dp[i][mask], transitions: skip i; or if v = a[i] not in mask, take c or c+1 copies starting at i -> jump to pos[v][idx+take-1]+1.
3. Feasible iff some state reaches mask 255; value 8c + max extras.
4. Feasibility is monotone in c: binary search c in [1, n/8].
5. Baseline answer (c = 0) = number of distinct values.
complexity: O(n * 256 * log n) time, O(n * 256) space

brief: Purple 2x2 bricks at (x_i, height h) with x_i increasing (gaps >= 2); add the minimum number of bricks (centers on y=0) so every brick off the ground rests on another with positive overlap.
key_idea: Each brick needs a column of h supports; two columns can share a brick once they meet: a group l..r merges at depth t = ceil((x_r - x_l)/2), saving the h - t + 1 bricks below; interval DP over merges plus a partition DP into groups.
solution:
1. dp[i][i] = h.
2. For l < r with t = ceil((x_r - x_l)/2) <= h: dp[l][r] = min over split m of dp[l][m] + dp[m+1][r] - (h - t + 1).
3. best[r] = min over l of best[l-1] + dp[l][r] (groups that never merge).
4. Answer best[n]. (Verified on all four samples; not proven here.)

brief: Count arrangements b of the multiset a (n even, n <= 5000) with b1 < b2 > b3 < b4 > ... < bn and b2 < b4 < ... < bn, mod 998244353.
key_idea: Even positions are increasing peaks p_1 < ... < p_k; odd slot 1 needs a value < p_1 and slot i+1 needs < p_i. Process distinct values in decreasing order with state j = #peaks chosen: a peak opens a slot for smaller values, other copies fill already-open slots (C(free, copies)).
solution:
1. Group equal values, process descending; processed = #elements already handled.
2. opened(j) = max(0, j-1) + [j == k] (the last peak p_1 opens two slots); free = opened(j) - (processed - j).
3. Not a peak: dp[j] * C(free, c).
4. One copy becomes the next peak: dp[j+1] += dp[j] * C(free, c-1) (copies must use slots of larger peaks).
5. Answer dp[k] after all values.
